issues.sym: Usually nothing at all. You may simply get a recall letter. The danger only shows up in a crash that sets off the driver airbag.
issues.why: GM found that the driver frontal airbag inflator on many Astras built from April 2007 to July 2008 can build too much pressure when it fires and burst, throwing metal pieces at the people inside. Recall 16V-063 (GM number 28810) replaces the driver airbag module.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls today. If the recall is open, call a GM dealer and have the free airbag module replacement done before driving the car more than you must.

issues.t: Check engine light and rough running from cam phaser solenoids
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft timing codes such as P000A, P000B, P0011 or P0014. Some cars feel flat, hesitate, idle roughly or make a light rattle.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine moves its camshafts with oil-controlled actuators. Tiny filter screens in the actuator solenoids can crack or clog, so the cam timing reacts slowly and the computer flags it. GM bulletin PIP-4644 describes this, and owners report the solenoids themselves failing too.
issues.next: Make sure the oil is full and fresh, then have the codes read. A shop can test and replace the intake or exhaust cam solenoid, which is a modest repair. Keep up with oil changes so the screens stay clean.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil pack
issues.sym: Flashing or steady check engine light, shaking at idle, loss of power or the engine cutting out, sometimes a no-start.
issues.why: The Astra uses a single coil pack that sits on top of all four spark plugs. It is the most reported repair on the car in owner surveys and tends to fail anywhere from about 30,000 to over 100,000 miles.
issues.next: If the check engine light is flashing, drive gently and get it checked soon, because misfires can overheat the catalytic converter. Replacing the coil pack and checking the spark plugs at the same time usually fixes it.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal sensor failure causing loss of power
issues.sym: The car stops speeding up when you press the gas, drops into a low-power mode, or responds unevenly to the pedal. The check engine light often comes on.
issues.why: The gas pedal has an electronic position sensor instead of a cable. On Astras this sensor, and in some cases its wiring connector at the firewall, can send bad signals, so the engine computer cuts power to protect itself. Some owners needed the pedal replaced more than once.
issues.next: Losing power in traffic is dangerous. If it happens, signal, move out of traffic and stop safely. Have the codes read before more highway driving; the usual fix is a new pedal assembly and a check of its wiring.

issues.t: Shifter won't go into Park or Reverse, or car rolls in Park
issues.sym: The lever won't go into Park or Reverse, the key won't come out, the car creeps while in Park, or the car seems stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Owners and dealers have traced several of these cases to a worn or broken bushing where the shift cable connects to the transmission, so the lever no longer moves the transmission into the gear shown. Others needed internal transmission work.
issues.next: Don't trust Park until this is fixed. Always set the parking brake and turn the wheels toward the curb. Have the shift cable and bushing checked first, since that is a small part.

issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm, the compressor rattles or squeals, or the A/C suddenly quits. In rare cases a seized compressor can throw the drive belt.
issues.why: The A/C compressor is the most common non-engine failure reported by Astra owners. It wears out internally or its clutch fails, often between about 30,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Turn the A/C off if you hear grinding. Have a shop check the system. A seized compressor usually means replacing it along with the drier and a recharge.

issues.sym: A whine, rubbing or chattering from the right side of the engine. If the belt breaks, the engine shuts off and won't restart.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine uses a rubber timing belt with a tensioner and idler pulley. They wear with age and miles. If the belt slips or snaps, the valves can hit the pistons and ruin the engine; one owner needed a replacement engine after a timing belt problem.
issues.next: If you don't know when the belt was last changed, have it inspected and replaced on the schedule in your owner's manual. Replace the tensioner and pulleys with it.

issues.t: Overheating from failed radiator cooling fan
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs in traffic or on hot days, coolant boils over, or the fan never comes on.
issues.why: The electric radiator fan motor can seize or its fuse can blow. Without the fan, the engine overheats at low speeds. One owner's fan failed at about 92,000 miles and the engine dumped its coolant.
issues.next: If the gauge goes into the red, pull over and shut the engine off. Don't open the hot coolant cap. Have the fan, its fuse and the coolant level checked before driving again.

issues.t: Thermostat stuck open or slow warm-up
issues.sym: The temperature gauge stays low, the heater blows lukewarm, fuel use goes up, and the check engine light may show P0128 or P0116.
issues.why: The thermostat can stick open, so the engine never fully warms up. Owners report replacing it at anywhere from a few thousand to well over 100,000 miles.
issues.next: It is not urgent, but get it fixed so the engine runs efficiently and the heater works in winter.

issues.sym: Erratic idle, hesitation, poor throttle response or reduced-power mode with the check engine light on.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the electronic throttle body, and some units fail outright. Owners report cleaning fixing mild cases, while replacement is much more costly when the part fails.
issues.next: Ask the shop to try a throttle body cleaning and relearn first. If the unit itself has failed, replacement is the fix.

issues.t: Check engine light from mass airflow sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with an airflow code such as P0101, sometimes with rough running or worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The mass airflow (MAF) sensor measures air going into the engine. It is one of the most commonly replaced sensors on the Astra, often between about 50,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the code read. A shop may try cleaning the sensor and checking the air filter before replacing it.

issues.t: Check engine light from fuel filler cap or pipe (EVAP leak)
issues.sym: Check engine light with EVAP leak codes such as P0442, P0455 or P0456. The car drives normally.
issues.why: GM bulletin 08-06-04-024 covers Astras that set these codes because of a faulty fuel fill cap or filler pipe. Several owners had the cap and pipe replaced, some early in the car's life.
issues.next: Check that the gas cap clicks tight. If the light stays on, have the EVAP codes read and the cap and filler neck inspected.

issues.sym: Check engine light (often P0496), rough idle after refueling, or hard starting right after filling the tank.
issues.why: The purge solenoid lets fuel vapor from the charcoal canister into the engine. When it sticks open, vapor flows at the wrong time.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed. The valve is a fairly inexpensive part on most cars.

issues.sym: Check engine light with an oxygen sensor or heater code, sometimes with worse fuel economy.
issues.why: The upstream and downstream oxygen sensors are among the most frequently replaced parts on the Astra in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have the code read to see which sensor is at fault. A bad sensor won't strand you but can hurt fuel economy and emissions.

issues.sym: A loud rumble, ticking or blatting under the car, especially on acceleration, and sometimes an oxygen sensor code.
issues.why: The flexible woven section of the front exhaust pipe cracks with age and heat. It is the second most common repair group in TrueDelta's Astra survey.
issues.next: Exhaust leaks under the cabin can let fumes in. Don't drive with the windows up and a strong exhaust smell; get the leak repaired.

issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0420, sluggish acceleration, or a rattle from under the car.
issues.why: Several owners report converters failing or melting, often after a misfire, a bad coil or a failed sensor that let unburned fuel into the exhaust.
issues.next: Fix any misfire first, or a new converter can fail too. Then have the converter tested before replacing it.

issues.sym: Check engine light with an intake runner or tuning valve code, sometimes with a slight loss of power.
issues.why: The plastic intake manifold has a built-in valve that changes the air path. It can bind or its sensor can fail, and the usual fix is a new manifold.
issues.next: This is rarely urgent. Have the code confirmed and ask for a quote on the manifold.

issues.t: Camshaft position sensor failure or oil seep
issues.sym: Check engine light with a cam sensor code, hard starting, or a small oil seep around the sensor.
issues.why: The cam position sensors on the 1.8L engine fail fairly often, and their seals can leak a little oil.
issues.next: Have the code read. The sensors are inexpensive and quick to replace.

issues.t: Drive belt squeal or broken belt from tensioner or alternator pulley
issues.sym: Squealing or chirping from the engine, especially with the A/C on, or a sudden loss of charging and power steering if the belt breaks.
issues.why: Many Astra owners report the accessory belt tensioner, idler pulley or alternator pulley wearing early, some within the first 20,000 miles. GM covered the alternator pulley under a bulletin for some owners.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on or the steering gets heavy, stop safely; the belt may be off. Otherwise have the tensioner and pulleys checked when you hear squealing.

issues.sym: Battery light, dimming lights, a dead battery or the car stalling.
issues.why: Alternator failures are a common repair on Astras, often past about 75,000 miles.
issues.next: If the battery light comes on, head somewhere safe and get it tested. The car can die once the battery runs down.

issues.t: Horn and steering wheel buttons stop working
issues.sym: The horn works only sometimes or not at all, often after rain. Steering wheel radio or cruise buttons may stop working or do the wrong thing.
issues.why: Owners and NHTSA complaints describe horn faults and failures of the steering column module that carries the horn and wheel buttons. GM issued a bulletin for the horn on some cars.
issues.next: A working horn is a safety item. Have the horn circuit, clockspring and steering column module checked.

issues.sym: Power windows, door locks, mirrors or even the radio stop working, sometimes one after another. One owner found a burnt section of the door harness.
issues.why: The wires that flex between the door and the body can wear through and short. This is the most reported problem on CarComplaints for the 2008 Astra.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic or see smoke from a door, pull the fuse for that circuit and get it repaired. Ask the shop to inspect all the door harness boots.

issues.sym: The fan works only on high or quits altogether, so you get little air from the vents.
issues.why: The blower motor or its speed resistor fails. Working only on the highest speed points to the resistor.
issues.next: Clear vents matter for defrosting in winter. Have the resistor checked first, since it is cheaper than the motor.

issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and changes when you turn.
issues.why: Front wheel bearings wear out on some Astras, with owners reporting replacements from about 60,000 miles on.
issues.next: A bad bearing gets louder over time and can eventually affect steering. Have it checked soon and replaced.

issues.t: Clunking from sway bar links or tie rods
issues.sym: Clunks or knocks over bumps, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Stabilizer bar end links, tie rod ends and ball joints are common wear items on the Astra.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Loose tie rods or ball joints affect steering and should be fixed promptly, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or wearing out early (manual)
issues.sym: Engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the clutch pedal feels different, or shifting becomes hard.
issues.why: Several manual-transmission owners replaced the clutch, sometimes with the flywheel and slave cylinder, between about 50,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: A slipping clutch only gets worse. Plan the repair before it leaves you unable to drive.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinding or losing a gear
issues.sym: Grinding, whining or a gear (often second) that won't engage or locks up.
issues.why: A few owners of manual Astras had internal gear or bearing failures that needed a replacement transmission.
issues.next: Stop driving it hard and get it checked; a failing gearbox can lock up.

issues.sym: The tire pressure light flashes or stays on even though the tires are properly inflated.
issues.why: Tire pressure sensors in the wheels and their programming cause repeat warnings on many Astras.
issues.next: Check all four tires with a gauge first. If they are fine, have the sensors scanned and replaced or reprogrammed.

issues.sym: A low-coolant warning appears even though the reservoir is full.
issues.why: The coolant level sensor in the reservoir fails on some Astras.
issues.next: Check the coolant level with the engine cold. If it is full, the sensor is likely bad. If it is low, look for a leak.

issues.sym: The steering wheel suddenly gets very hard to turn while driving or when parked.
issues.why: NHTSA has several complaints about sudden loss of power steering assist on the Astra, which uses an electric pump for its power steering.
issues.next: You can still steer, but it takes much more effort. Slow down, pull over safely and have the steering system, fuse and pump checked before driving far.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover or oil cooler
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or oil on the top of the engine.
issues.why: Valve cover gaskets and the oil cooler seals on the 1.8L engine can seep as the car ages.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the source found. Oil dripping on the exhaust can smoke.

issues.sym: The outside mirror glass comes loose or falls out.
issues.why: The mirror glass is clipped to a heated backing plate, and the clips or adhesive let go on many Astras.
issues.next: Replace it before driving much, so you can see beside the car.

issues.sym: A window grinds, moves slowly or stops; you may hear a click from inside the door.
issues.why: Window regulators and motors wear out, especially the rear ones.
issues.next: Have the door opened and the regulator checked. Keep the window closed and the car covered if it won't go up.
